title: World Genome (v0)
description: The complete, deterministic recipe for one world. A world is NOT code written by hand; it is the deterministic expansion of this genome by a versioned grammar. Two invariants: (1) expansion is a pure function -- genome + grammar_version fully determine the world, bit for bit; (2) worlds are immutable -- evolution produces DESCENDANT genomes, never in-place edits. Historical evidence binds to the exact content hash of the world that generated it, forever.

world_id.description: equal to content_hash prefix; worlds are content-addressed

grammar_version.description: identity of the generative grammar that expands this genome. The grammar lives INSIDE the engine release identity: a grammar change is a release change. The world-phylogeny discipline applies at THIS level -- grammar versions are earned by measured failures of their predecessors.

generation_seed.description: seed for the deterministic expansion; with grammar_version, fully determines the mechanics DAG

parent_ids.description: zero parents = de novo sample from the grammar; one = mutation; two = recombination (subgraph splice). Never empty for a mutated world.

mutation_history.description: ordered mutation operations that produced this genome from its parent(s). Empty for de novo worlds.

target.description: node id in the mechanics DAG

mechanics_manifest.description: The expanded mechanics DAG: typed composition of generative primitives. This is the EXPANSION output, recorded for audit; the genome (grammar_version + generation_seed + mutations) is the authority, and re-expansion must reproduce this manifest bit-for-bit or the world is invalid (determinism breach).

primitive.description: primitive name within the family, e.g. REGISTER_BANK, LINEAR_MOD, REGIME_SWITCH, DELAY_QUEUE, PROJECTION, XOR_MIX, SHARED_CONTENTION

params.description: integer parameters only. FLOATS ARE BANNED from world physics (cross-host determinism).

n_slots.description: player slots. Slot roles may be asymmetric; the INTERFACE never labels which mechanisms are other players.

horizon_class.description: declared consequence-delay class, derived mechanically from the DAG (max delay-queue depth, regime-switch period). USED FOR QUALIFICATION-TIER STRATIFICATION so staged early death does not silently select against slow-developing strategies. Never visible to players.

stochasticity.description: SEEDED_STOCHASTIC draws exclusively from named seed streams derived from the episode seed; there is no other entropy source anywhere in a world

interface_manifest.description: The player-facing contract. SEMANTIC QUARANTINE APPLIES: opaque integer vectors only; no names, labels, units, or documentation cross this boundary; channel order is permuted per-world by seed.

mixing.description: seeded invertible integer mixing applied at the boundary to destroy designer channel decomposition. Mixing level is an EXPERIMENTAL ARM, not a constant: how much of any result depends on our decomposition is a measured quantity.

resource_constraints.description: Authoritative budgets enforced by the engine, not by politeness. Step budgets are the scientific quantity; wall-clock is a safety kill only and never appears in any statistic.

player_step_budget.description: VM steps per player per encounter

player_persist_limit.description: bytes of state a player may carry between ticks

wallclock_safety_ms.description: SAFETY KILL ONLY; an encounter killed by wall-clock is recorded as INFRASTRUCTURE_ABORT, never as a player outcome

runtime_hash.description: build-derived hash of the world-runtime code (expansion + step function). Lives inside the engine release identity.

content_hash.description: hash over the canonical serialization of every field above except world_id and content_hash itself

$comment: NON-GOALS: (a) no field may carry a human-language description of what the world 'is about' -- that text lives in Daedalus-side instrumentation OUTSIDE the genome; (b) no difficulty rating, no quality score -- discrimination is measured empirically by the reference battery, never asserted; (c) horizon_class is mechanically derived, not authored. FOSSIL RULE: no genome is ever deleted; boring worlds define the landscape against which a bump is visible.
